memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Levitical priests—indeed, the whole tribe of Levi—are to have no allotment or inheritance with Israel. They shall live on the food offerings presented to the Lord, for that is their inheritance. They shall have no inheritance among their fellow Israelites; the Lord is their inheritance, as he promised them. - Deut 18:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As the other tribes received portions of land, the tribe of Levi received something different, and something greater. They were given no territory of their own. Instead, God Himself declared, "The Lord is their inheritance." While their brothers looked to fields and vineyards, the Levites were to look directly to God as their portion.

At first this might seem like they were being left out. But look closer. God was not withholding good from the Levites; He was giving them the best thing of all, Himself. Their security did not rest in land they owned but in the God who owned everything.

This speaks tenderly to every believer. In Christ, we too can say the Lord is our portion. Our deepest security is not in what we possess, our savings, our property, our achievements, but in God Himself. Possessions can be lost overnight; God never fails. The psalmist echoed this joy when he said God was his portion forever (Ps 73:26). When our hearts learn to find their treasure in God rather than in things, we gain a stability the world cannot shake. What if the Lord Himself, not what He gives, became your greatest treasure? Where are you tempted to find your security in possessions rather than in God?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you find your deepest security today?
2. What would it mean to call the Lord your portion?
3. How might loosening your grip on possessions free your heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are my greatest treasure and my truest security. Teach me to find my portion in You, not in the things I own. Amen.
